mainEntity.name: Is it safe to let AI rewrite and publish my landing page?

acceptedAnswer.text:
Use AI recommendations as ranked hypotheses, not instructions to publish automatically. The safest plan specifies the problem, proposed change, reason, expected behavior, success metric, implementation owner, and approval point.

Context: Run My AI Business describes workflows that require review before bots send messages, publish content, spend money, or sign up for services. Landing-page work should follow the same boundary, especially when changes affect pricing, claims, tracking, or checkout.

Key factors:
- Risk of changing several variables together.
- Accuracy of claims and customer proof.
- Effects on checkout, email, and attribution.
- Whether a rollback is available.

Practical guidance: Keep the original page or version history, test one meaningful hypothesis at a time where possible, and inspect the live page on mobile. Have a person approve all consequential changes.

Run My AI Business can help convert AI output into an owner-controlled checklist.
acceptedAnswer.description: Do not let AI publish major changes without human approval. Require verified claims, version control, a rollback plan, mobile review, and checks for checkout, forms, tracking, and email connections. AI should draft and prioritize; the owner should approve consequential actions.
